source: FAO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, "Swine Health Management, Volume 3: Frequently Asked Questions on Pig Biosecurity and Disease Reporting", RAP Publication 2012/27, Bangkok, 2012. Acknowledgements credit national focal points from Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand and Viet Nam as contributors.
text: When bringing new pigs onto a farm: start with pigs of good health status from a reliable, inspectable source rather than an unknown trader or mixed market lot; buying directly from a single farm carries less disease risk than buying from an auction market or collection point where animals from many origins are mixed together; transport new pigs in a vehicle that has been cleaned and disinfected beforehand; and quarantine and allow the new pigs to acclimatize for 15-30 days in a separate area before mixing them with the existing herd - this both lets a farmer observe for signs of disease and lets the new pigs adjust to the farm's feed, water and environment before being expected to perform normally.
